correctness.rationale: For R_r(x,y) meaning distance <r, R_r composed with R_s is R_(r+s) on either dense subset: split the segment in ratio r:s, where both inequalities have slack, and approximate the split point in the subset. For r>s, inclusion of the open s-neighborhood of y in the open r-neighborhood of x is equivalent to d(x,y)≤r−s. The forward metric bound uses the triangle inequality with one strict leg. If d>r−s, choose t between max(0,r−d) and s and extend the ray from x through y by t. The two strict witness inequalities persist on a dense-set approximation. A bijection preserves compositions and inclusions of the corresponding neighborhood sets, so preserves the closed thresholds at all positive differences of positive semigroup elements. Every positive element of Z a+Z b is such a difference (add a common positive semigroup element if one side is zero). For irrational a/b this subgroup has arbitrarily small positive elements by pigeonholing multiples modulo one radius, and is therefore dense; comparisons at its positive elements force exact distance equality, including boundary cases. The unique extension to the completions is isometric with closed dense image, hence surjective and affine by Mazur–Ulam. At rational ratio the scaled fractional-part square map is strictly increasing and continuous also at tile endpoints, and commutes with every integer translation in the common unit. Monotonicity then preserves all the strict integer-unit thresholds. It fixes 0 and the unit and does not fix their midpoint, so is nonaffine. None of these universal conclusions depend on the supplied finite rational example check, which was inspected but not executed.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact criterion for universally recovering a metric from just two qualitative relations on a dense sample, with no dimensional or strict-convexity assumption. It identifies commensurability as the obstruction and produces full affine rigidity on the completions. The known scaled counterexample makes the criterion sharp but is not the source of its value.
